primary_source.what_it_is_our_words: The authentic text is the Official Journal edition on EUR-Lex. Its licence is not on the act; it is the EU's reuse regime: Commission Decision 2011/833/EU, applied to EUR-Lex content by the EUR-Lex legal notice, with EU-owned web content additionally under CC BY 4.0 per the Commission's legal notice.
primary_source.note: The Directive text itself was NOT re-fetched in this lane — R1 fetched the DG EMPL page at #236 (fetch-receipts slug 'eaa', 171,551 bytes OK). This lane's job was the licence, which lives elsewhere.

licence.name: EU reuse regime — Commission Decision 2011/833/EU (reuse of Commission documents), with EU-owned web content under CC BY 4.0 per the Commission legal notice
licence.read_from: the Decision's own text (legislation.gov.uk King's Printer copy, derived from EUR-Lex on IP completion day, unamended) + the Commission legal notice 'Copyright notice' section
licence.quote_le_15_words: for commercial or non-commercial purposes under the conditions laid down in Article 6
licence.second_quote_le_15_words: the obligation for the reuser to acknowledge the source of the documents
licence.second_quote_locus: Decision 2011/833/EU, Article 6(2)(a); 6(2)(b) adds 'not to distort the original meaning or message'
licence.third_quote_le_15_words: reuse is allowed, provided appropriate credit is given and changes are indicated
licence.corroboration_quote_le_15_words: content derived from EUR-Lex, reused under the terms of the Commission Decision 2011/833/EU
licence.grants_our_words: Reuse for any purpose, commercial included, free, without asking, on two conditions: name the source and do not distort the meaning. Web content the EU owns is additionally CC BY 4.0.
licence.forbids_our_words: Distorting the text; reuse 'calculated to deceive or to defraud' (Art. 2(4)); logos, names and trademarks are excluded (Art. 2(2)(a)); third-party-rights material is excluded (Art. 2(2)(b)).
licence.ai_clause: none in the Decision; the Commission notice has an AI section but it is about the Commission's OWN use of AI in content creation, not a restriction on reusers

permits_us: reproduce — verbatim Directive text with the source acknowledged and the meaning undistorted; paraphrase likewise (changes indicated)
why_our_words: The legal set that s237-D4 puts first was missing its one directive. The reuse regime is explicit and the conditions are two: credit and fidelity. That makes the EAA the same tier as DSA Article 25 and the EDPB guidelines, which R1 already put in 'safe now' on the same policy.
unproven: The EUR-Lex legal notice's OWN sentence applying the Decision to legislative texts (acts of the Parliament and Council are not, strictly, 'Commission documents'). Three routes to EUR-Lex failed in this fetcher; the legislation.gov.uk footer and Decision recital 7 ('the full corpus of Union law freely available online') corroborate but are not the notice. Price: one browser-client render of https://eur-lex.europa.eu/content/legal-notice/legal-notice.html — lane G proved that route at #237 (~2K tokens).
R1's UNPROVEN 3 (the 28 June 2025 application date) is untouched by this lane — not a licence question.

pitfalls.what: Fidelity is a licence CONDITION here, not a nicety: an obligation node that paraphrases the EAA into something it does not say breaches Art. 6(2)(b) as well as misleading a client.
pitfalls.owner: obligation-node author; a diff-against-source check on obligation nodes would catch it

pitfalls.what: 'Source acknowledged' must survive the generation chain — a generated screen brief that quotes the EAA without the source line loses the grant.

The fetcher/host mismatch will recur for every EUR-Lex family: anyone re-verifying the DSA, EAA or EDPB from the sandbox will get an empty body and may write 'blocked'. The runbook answer is lane G's: use the browser client.
